title: Convergent request metadata router and fanout adapter
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a lightweight in-process request metadata router that normalizes upstream headers/baggage/identifiers and fans them out to tracing, metrics, and log pipelines with minimal runtime overhead. Goal is a single SDK middleware primitive that: 1) normalizes trace context to OpenTelemetry / legacy carriers and Redwood x-req-id, 2) exposes a compact API for downstream services to read/write canonical attributes, 3) supports asynchronous fanout to observability sinks with backpressure and graceful degradation, and 4) reconciles sampling decisions across tracing and metrics to avoid telemetry duplication. This ticket covers design, API prototypes for Go/Node/Python SDKs, integration test harness, and an initial canary rollout on staging routes.

acceptance_criteria: Middleware exposes a Read/Write canonical attribute API across Go/Node/Python SDKs
Normalization rules map common carriers (OTEL, B3, W3C Trace Context) to Redwood canonical keys
End-to-end integration tests validate sampling reconciliation behaviour under 0%/50%/100% synthetic sampling
Per-request overhead median < 0.5ms and p99 < 5ms on benchmark hardware
Async fanout has bounded queue with durable metrics: fanout_latency_ms, fanout_dropped_count
Canary rollout in staging running for 48 hours with no increase in 5xx or latency SLO violations
implementation_notes: Normalize on ingress: convert headers to canonical map immediately and store in request context
Deterministic reconcile: compute sampling tags once before any async work and attach decision to canonical map
Fanout workers: bounded pool with token-bucket backpressure; on overflow, increment fanout_dropped_count and emit a structured log
Fallback: if fanout sinks are unavailable, continue request path without blocking; provide metric and optional span annotation
SDK adapters: provide idiomatic middleware hooks (Express/Koa for Node, net/http for Go, ASGI for Python) and a light weight in-memory carrier API
Testing: harness to inject synthetic upstream carriers and assert normalized output emitted to OTLP collector mock
